newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn expects to meet criteria despite EMU poll.
newsitem.headline: Bonn expects to meet criteria despite EMU poll.

text.p: The Finance Ministry said on Wednesday it still expected Germany to qualify for the start of European monetary union, despite the doubts of many economists.

"The ministry expects to meet the criteria," a ministry spokeswoman told Reuters in response to the news agency's poll showing many economists expect Germany to miss the Maastricht Treaty requirements.

Germany was likely to fall just short of the requirements for a deficit-to-gross domestic product ratio of 3.0 percent and a total debt-to-GDP ratio of 60 percent, according to a Reuters poll of 32 economists across Europe.
They predicted Germany's deficit ratio would be 3.5 percent and its debt ratio 62 percent of GDP.
Bonn last month in its annual economic report forecast a deficit/GDP ratio of 2.9 percent, the finance ministry spokeswoman said. "That still stands."
Bonn also did not expect EMU criteria to be eased, should Germany fall short, the spokeswoman said.
"The criteria is 3.0 percent, not 3.1 percent or 3.2 percent, and the ministry expects Germany to qualify with 2.9 percent," she said.
Some economists polled by Reuters suggested political considerations could override the financial criteria, should Germany and France fail to qualify.
